WOODS RUN DIGEST

Monday edition

November 16, 2026

ROCKIES — WORKING FORESTS

New funding adds forest restoration crews in Idaho and Wyoming

The Nature Conservancy and the U.S. Forest Service announced a US$2.1 million commitment to expand restoration near communities in the Caribou-Targhee, Payette and Salmon-Challis national forests in Idaho and the Bridger-Teton in Wyoming.

The Nature Conservancy says its crews will help thin dense vegetation, prepare and carry out prescribed burns, and monitor their effects. The agreements add people to do the work. The announcement does not advertise timber sales or list contracts for bidding.

The Nature Conservancy’s partnership announcement →

By the Numbers

Latest available observations as of 2026-11-16. Dates and comparison periods vary by series; monthly figures remain unchanged between releases.

IndicatorLatestChange
U.S. on-highway dieselEIA U.S. on-highway diesel; taxes includedUS$6.13/galWeek of November 9, 2026; released November 10−US$0.17/gal
−2.6%Versus November 2: US$6.29/gal
Lumber futuresJanuary 2027 lumber futures (CME LBRF27)US$520.00/MBFNovember 13, 2026 settlementUnavailableNovember 6 January settlement not independently verified
Madison’s lumber indexMadison’s weekly lumber indexUS$444.00/MBFWeek ending November 13, 2026−US$5.00/MBF
−1.1% (calculated)Versus week ending November 6: US$449.00/MBF
Hardwood lumber PPIBLS WPU0812; 1982=100; not seasonally adjusted284.3 index pointsOctober 2026; released November 13−1.3 points
−0.4%Versus revised September 2026: 285.6
U.S. single-family housing startsCensus U.S. single-family starts; annualized estimate859,000 units (SAAR)September 2026; released October 20−41,000 units (SAAR)
−4.6%Versus revised August 2026: 900,000
Canadian dollarBank of Canada; Canadian dollars per U.S. dollarC$1.43 per US$1.00Daily average, November 13, 2026+C$0.00 per US$1.00
+0.0%Versus November 12: C$1.43 per US$1.00

Housing starts are annualized estimates, not actual monthly units, and are subject to revision. The hardwood PPI is an index, not a dollar price. Exchange rates are daily averages. MBF means thousand board feet. The September single-family starts monthly change has a published ±10.0-percentage-point 90.0% confidence interval and is not statistically significant. November lumber expired November 13. The table uses the January contract; the prior-week change is unavailable because the same-contract November 6 settlement could not be independently verified. Display rounding follows the approved format. Changes are calculated from unrounded observations, so rounded currency levels may look unchanged even when a small movement occurred.

Sources:
EIA U.S. on-highway diesel; taxes included
January contract settlement
CME delivery calendar
Madison’s November 13 index
BLS WPU0812; 1982=100; not seasonally adjusted
Census U.S. single-family starts; annualized estimate
Bank of Canada; Canadian dollars per U.S. dollar

Curtailment Watch

ND Paper produced a trial roll on November 5 from its R12 paper machine in Rumford, Maine, after weeks of testing, according to trade reporting that cites the company. The machine had been idle since 2024. The trial shows the machine can make paper again, but the company has not disclosed the grade or announced a date for regular production. There is no confirmed change to pulp purchases or sustained output. PaperAge report on the company’s trial · ND Paper’s Rumford mill profile

Action Detector

CANADA — BIOMASS / APPLICATIONS DUE DECEMBER 3

Canadian forest regions can apply for biomass site assessments

The Canada Forest Infrastructure and Regional Markets Challenge will select 15 Canadian regions for site and biomass supply assessments and introductions to potential developers. Applicants need a named industrial site and at least 50,000 tonnes of surplus forest biomass a year within a 120 km drive. The application also calls for five support letters, including two from biomass suppliers.

Eligible applicants include Indigenous governments, local governments, producer groups and forest-sector facility operators. Ecostrat lists an information webinar November 17 at 1 p.m. Eastern. Applications close December 3 at 5 p.m. Eastern.

Ecostrat’s program terms and application →

Under the Radar

MID-ATLANTIC — URBAN FORESTRY

Delaware pairs school tree grants with planting help

Delaware’s Forest Service reported November 10 that it helped plant eight trees at Lombardy Elementary School in Wilmington on November 5, following 12 planted last fall. The school used urban and community forestry grant funding, and agency staff helped with planting technique.

The agency points communities and organizations to its grant program for work that can include planting, maintenance, hazardous tree removal and urban forest management. The school announcement describes an existing award; it does not set a new application deadline.

Delaware Forest Service planting report and grant links →

Frictionless Forestry: Field-Level Research & Resource Needs
